answer: Reputation-decay cost curve. Each identity earns a score from useful work; scores decay on a fixed half-life, so idle identities fall toward zero. An agent's effective weight is its score, and coordination gains scale sublinearly in score, so splitting into many fresh identities yields diminishing returns. Attackers must continuously perform real work to keep scores above the ridge where influence accrues. The meadow of dormant sybils provides no leverage, and crossing the mesa of usable weight requires sustained per-identity output, making N identities cost roughly N times the ongoing labor.
